decisions: A semantic table retains all product fields and untruncated names for comparison; a labeled horizontal scroll region keeps it usable on narrow screens.
A collapsed advanced filter panel combines status, category and inclusive low-stock filtering with case-insensitive name/SKU search.
Read-only rows explain the permission restriction. Both editor opening and submission enforce the supplied canEdit value.
A native modal dialog provides an editor with explicit keyboard focus looping and focus restoration after save.
Invalid saves retain all field values, mark individual fields and announce an error summary. Unsaved closing uses a browser confirmation; reload/navigation uses beforeunload.
Save updates only the in-memory collection, refreshes counts/filter results, and announces the product saved.
Brand token values were preserved. System fonts, local CSS and text symbols supply all visuals.

passes.work: Implemented the complete interface and ran browser checks. Reviewed desktop, tablet, mobile, and mobile editor screenshots. Initial width assertions incorrectly assumed scrollbars consume no viewport width.
Corrected the scrollbar-aware assertions, improved save focus restoration and made reverse Tab wrap explicitly inside the modal. Final verification passed all 33 assertions.

command_notes: All commands ran in the assigned A directory except the absolute common-task read. Source files and the browser harness were written with shell heredocs and Python Path edits; their exact resulting content is retained in this directory. checks.mjs contains the exact Chrome DevTools calls, assertions, test inputs and screenshot sizes. No Git commands, external references, design skills, other runs or repository documentation were used.
unsupported_production_requirements: No backend persistence: reload restores the original supplied data.
No authenticated user service or server-side authorization: supplied canEdit permissions are enforced only in this local interface.
No multi-user conflict handling, synchronization, audit history, or production loading/error transport.
limitations: Verification used one local headless Chrome build; other browsers and assistive technologies were not manually tested.
The loading query state is intentionally stable for reproducible capture and does not transition automatically.
Narrow screens require horizontal table scrolling to reach later columns.
beforeunload is implemented, but browser-level navigation warning behavior was not independently exercised; editor discard confirmation was exercised.
No automated accessibility or contrast audit was run. Visual conclusions apply only to screenshots listed as visually reviewed.
cleanup: Verification Chrome closed and temporary .chrome-profile removed. Local HTTP server remains available on 127.0.0.1:9311 for controller captures.
